answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a stake released only slowly over time, like basalt forming under pressure: spawning thousands of fake agents becomes expensive because every identity ties up capital that cannot be reused elsewhere. Reputation then accrues only through verified completed work, marble-hard and slow to earn, so a newcomer cannot buy instant trust. Honest agents working the shared meadow of open tasks are rewarded, while detected sybils forfeit their stake and history, pushing the attacker's cost far above any reward from gaming the system.
